newsitem.title: USA: Senate confirms Slater as transportation secretary.
newsitem.headline: Senate confirms Slater as transportation secretary.

text.p: The Senate voted 98-0 Wednesday to confirm Rodney Slater to be secretary of transportation during President Clinton's second term.

Slater, 41, who has been head of the Transportation Department's Federal Highway Administration since 1993, will succeed Federico Pena as transportation chief. Clinton has nominated Pena to be energy secretary.

Slater has been a political ally of Clinton since the president was governor of Arkansas. He was named by Clinton to the Arkansas Highway Commission and later became its first African-American chairman.
Several senators warmly praised Slater as the right man to deal with problems facing the nation's transportation system.
Democrat Robert Byrd of West Virginia said the system had a backlog of unmet needs, such as deteriorated roads and highways, totalling more than $100 billion.

The Senate confirmed four of Clinton's nominations earlier: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, Defence Secretary William Cohen, Commerce Secretary William Daley and Housing and Urban Development Secretary Andrew Cuomo.

Other pending nominations in addition to Pena include Alexis Herman to be secretary of Labour, Anthony Lake to be director of the Central Intelligence Agency, Representative Bill Richardson to be ambassador to the United Nations, Janet Yellen to chair the Council of Economic Advisers and Charlene Barshefsky to be U.S. Trade Representative.
